dag.label: SELF-VERIFY — the coder builds its own verifier
dag.task: Write a complete ES module file: src/verify.js. Export one function: export function verify(code) { ... }. It must: (1) use the 'acorn' npm package (import * as acorn from 'acorn') to parse the code string with { ecmaVersion: 2022, sourceType: 'module' }; (2) catch parse errors and return { ok: false, error: err.message }; (3) return { ok: true } on success. No other exports. No stubs. Full implementation.
dag.context: This is a Cloudflare Worker module. acorn will be bundled by wrangler/esbuild from package.json. The function must handle both valid JS and invalid JS. Known-good test: 'function add(a,b){return a+b}' → {ok:true}. Known-bad test: 'function {{{' → {ok:false, error: <message>}.
post_apply_commands: node -e "import('./src/verify.js').then(m => { const r1 = m.verify('function add(a,b){return a+b}'); const r2 = m.verify('function {{{'); console.log('good:', JSON.stringify(r1), 'bad:', JSON.stringify(r2)); if (!r1.ok || r2.ok) process.exit(1); })"

It must: (1) parse body as { steps: [{task, context?, target?}], model? }; (2) loop steps sequentially; (3) for each step, call env.AI.run(model || '@cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct', { messages: [{role:'system', content: SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {role:'user', content: buildUserMsg(step)}], max_tokens:8192 }) where buildUserMsg concatenates context + target + task; (4) strip markdown fences from result.response; (5) call verify(patch) imported from './verify.js'; (6) carry patch forward as context for next step (prepend 'PREVIOUS STEP RESULT:\n' + patch); (7) collect {step_index, task, patch, verified, ms} per step; (8) return Response.json({ mission_id: 'MR-'+Date.now(), steps: results, all_verified: results.every(r=>r.verified) }). Export the function as named export. No auth check inside — auth is handled by caller. Imports: import { verify } from './verify.js'; SYSTEM_PROMPT is a const string at top of file with the 6 laws (L01-L06 as in current index.js).

dag.label: SWARM — /api/swarm (DAG wave-scheduler, 10 drones)
dag.note: Using llama-70b for this rung — it is the most complex logic in the build
dag.task: Write a complete handleSwarm(request, env) async function for a Cloudflare Worker. It must implement a topological wave-scheduler over a blueprint DAG. Spec: (1) parse body as { blueprint: MarchingOrder[], drones?: number } where MarchingOrder = { id, task, context?, target?, model?, depends_on?: string[], verify?: 'acorn'|'none', on_fail?: string, max_retries?: number }; (2) default drones=10; (3) build a results map: Map<id, {status:'PENDING'|'VERIFIED'|'FAILED', patch:string}>; (4) WAVE LOOP: while any PENDING orders: find wave = orders where status===PENDING AND all depends_on are VERIFIED; if wave empty but PENDING orders remain → return error 'circular dependency or blocked DAG'; cap wave to drones; fire wave with Promise.all: for each order in wave, call env.AI.run(order.model || '@cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct', { messages: build_messages(order, results), max_tokens:8192 }); strip fences; run verify(patch) if order.verify==='acorn' else {ok:true}; mark VERIFIED or FAILED; (5) carry context: build_messages resolves depends_on by prepending patches from results map; (6) return { mission_id:'SW-'+Date.now(), waves: waveCount, drones_used: max_wave_size, results: [{id, verified, patch, ms, drone_index}], all_verified: bool }. Import verify from './verify.js'. Export as named export handleSwarm.
dag.context: This runs inside a Cloudflare Worker. Promise.all with up to 10 env.AI.run calls is safe on Paid CF (Workers AI neuron allocation). Each env.AI.run call returns { response: string }. The DAG is acyclic — the wave loop terminates. depends_on = [] means no dependencies (fire immediately in wave 1).
